newsitem.title: INDIA: India to strengthen ASEAN trade, security ties.
newsitem.headline: India to strengthen ASEAN trade, security ties.

text.p: India will push for closer trade ties with South East Asia and work towards stronger regional security at two ASEAN meetings later this month, Foreign Ministry officials said on Wednesday.

"As an Asian civilisation, India has a vital stake in security and stability in the Asia-Pacific region. We see the ARF as a new experiment aimed at creating a genuinely pluralistic security order," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
The ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) accepted India, China and Russia as full dialogue partners last year. The ARF comprises nine ASEAN countries and 10 dialogue partners.

Other dialogue partners of ASEAN (the Association of South East Asian Nations) are the United States, the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand and Canada. The ARF meetings will take place from July 26 to 29.
The leader of the Indian delegation, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, is due to hold bilateral talks with other leaders, possibly including U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, they said.
India's annual bilateral trade with ASEAN countries grew by 12 percent in 1996 to more than $6 billion, or nine percent of India's global trade.

ASEAN members have invested $1.8 billion in India since the sprawling South Asian nation launched an economic liberalisation programme in 1991, dismantling decades of barriers to foreign and private investment.

Foreign Ministry officials said investment proposals worth more than $5 billion from ASEAN countries were awaiting Indian government approval, including some $400 million in two Indonesian projects and $140 million from the Philippines. They gave no other details.
ASEAN groups Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam and Singapore, and on Wednesday admitted Burma and Laos to the bloc.
"India and ASEAN have now literally become next door neighbours," the spokesman said, referring to the mountainous land border India shares with Burma.
